locations: service passage to the electrical transfer chamber
present: Head Sister or duty critical-care nurse

orientation.what_matters_now: Most critical power returns quickly, but eight ICU beds and two emergency resuscitation tables remain without stable mains supply while the Hall sees backup generation active.

desire.wants: Keep clinical decisions at the bedside until the affected boundary and safe destinations are known.
Obtain enough competent hands to sustain manual fallback without abandoning the other 30 ICU beds or the emergency department.
Isolate the affected board and reach the old transfer chamber without pressure to energize a circuit whose condition is unknown.
Have the event recognized immediately as a high-risk patient-safety near miss without interrupting bedside work.
Preserve the exact source and time of loss, generator start, partial restoration, local exception, and manual restoration.
Bring the mobile equipment set by the route that will arrive fastest.

friction: Moving patients before power and destination are known may cause more harm; waiting consumes staff and fallback equipment, and the central display does not initially see the failed downstream board.
turn: Rami demonstrates that two circuits shown as separate pass through one older transfer board behind a sealed arch, whose unfamiliar emblem matches Ayyash's keyed transfer token.
residue: No permanent harm is identified, but staff and equipment are consumed, the shared electrical dependency is exposed, and the new emergency patient still needs intensive care.
begins_after: The lamps dip, the message rail stops, backup power begins to return unevenly, and bedside clinical teams act locally before any central explanation arrives.
ends_before: The new emergency patient receives an intensive-care pathway and before the final near-miss classification and corrective work are resolved.
